summary: The blueprint broadly covers human pancreas but needs targeted refinements for lymphatic endothelium, mural/stromal resolution, and a few marker choices.

issues.description: The endothelial module captures blood vascular endothelium but lacks lymphatic endothelial coverage, an expected normal pancreatic support compartment in a broad tissue embedding.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a lymphatic endothelial module and either a separate plain axis or an endothelial-gated blood-vs-lymphatic refinement using markers such as LYVE1, PDPN, PROX1, FLT4, and CCL21 where supported.

issues.description: Pericyte and vascular smooth muscle programs are merged into one axis, blurring related but distinct mural populations.
issues.suggested_fix: Split or refine the mural compartment into pericyte-enriched and smooth-muscle-enriched modules/axes, or retain the broad mural axis only if paired with a gated pericyte-vs-smooth-muscle refinement.

issues.description: The blueprint has only one generic stellate/fibroblast axis and may conflate activated stellate/myofibroblast-like state with vascular smooth muscle because ACTA2/TAGLN are only in the merged mural module.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a stromal-gated refinement that separates quiescent pancreatic stellate/fibroblast identity from activated myofibroblast-like activation, using atlas-supported markers.

issues.description: The epsilon-cell module contains only GHRL. GHRL is canonical, but one-gene scoring is fragile for a very rare endocrine population.
issues.suggested_fix: Add additional literature-supported human pancreas ghrelin/epsilon-enriched markers, or keep GHRL but treat epsilon as a rare endocrine refinement rather than a full-resolution subtype.

issues.description: NRXN1 is more neuronal/synaptic than a canonical Schwann/glial marker and weakens an otherwise plausible Schwann/glial module.
issues.suggested_fix: Replace NRXN1 with a stronger atlas-supported peripheral glial/Schwann marker such as NGFR, ERBB3, MBP, GFRA3, or another supported marker.

out_of_scope: DOI correctness and IF-threshold verification were not re-checked in this Discriminator pass.
The REG-positive acinar state is acceptable as a healthy-atlas acinar refinement and does not need removal.
